summary.headline: A debt-light, cash-rich supplier to its parent, but the price is about 30% above fair value
summary.text: ACL Plastics PLC (APLA.N0000) makes the PVC compound that coats cables and sells almost all of it to its parent ACL Cables (65.2%) and sister company Kelani Cables. It had a record 2025/26 (revenue +17% to Rs 2.85bn, profit +72% to Rs 798mn, ROE 20%), and the six months to September 2026 were up again (revenue +16%, EPS Rs 10.72 against Rs 8.37). But the September quarter's gross margin fell to 24.9% from 31.3%, quarterly profit slipped 10%, and stock and money owed by the group jumped, so operating cash was −Rs 456mn in the half and the company borrowed Rs 221mn for the first time in years. Over half the equity (Rs 2.5bn, Rs 59.86 a share) sits in unit trusts, deposits and listed shares, which also supply a quarter to a third of profit. With the shared CAPM method the required return is 18.3% (beta 0.98), higher than the 16.5% used before, and the methods put fair value at about Rs 120 (was Rs 139). At Rs 156.25 the share is about 30% above it. Still a good business on the four tests (watch list), but I'd buy only at up to about Rs 102 and treat under Rs 90 as a strong buy.

modelsNote: All four methods come from scripts/valuation.py and are weighted equally. Growth check: assumed 3% / 5.5% / 6.5% against 4.8% supported (reinvestment rate 24.4% × return on capital 19.9% in 2025/26), all within 2 points. The DCF values the PVC business only and adds the treasury investments, because their gains sit in operating profit in the annual report but in finance income in the interims. Dividend model left out: at a 20% payout its value would rest on the payout assumed after year five. Cost of debt is the bond yield (no borrowings at either year end); debt weight only 3%.

fullText:
**Summary**

ACL Plastics PLC (APLA.N0000) makes cable-grade PVC compound and sells essentially all of it to its parent ACL Cables (65.21%) and sister company Kelani Cables. It is a good business on the four tests: ROE about 20%, almost no debt, no loss in ten years, and profit has mostly turned into cash. But at Rs 156.25 (CSE close, 20 November 2026) the share is about 30% above my fair value of Rs 119.77. Buy price Rs 101.80 (fair value less 15%); strong buy Rs 89.82 (less 25%). Category: watch list (good business, price too high).

**What changed since the 11 November analysis**

- Fair value Rs 139 → Rs 119.77; buy Rs 118 → Rs 101.80; strong buy Rs 104 → Rs 89.82.
- The required return now comes from the shared CAPM method: beta 0.98 (specialty chemicals), cost of equity 18.3% (was a hand-set 16.5%). That is most of the fall.
- Long-run growth 6–7% → 4–5%, the same in every method.
- New: a DCF of the PVC business plus the treasury investments (replacing "operating profit × P/E plus cash"), and a justified P/E. Growth check, management and shareholder sections added.

**Latest results**

- Six months to September 2026: revenue Rs 1,526mn (+16%), profit Rs 452mn (+28%), EPS Rs 10.72 (Rs 8.37). Finance income Rs 170mn, of which Rs 77mn unrealised unit-trust gains and Rs 48mn unrealised exchange gains.
- September quarter: revenue Rs 788mn (+28%) but gross margin 24.9% (31.3%), profit Rs 157mn (−10%), EPS Rs 3.73 (Rs 4.13).
- Balance sheet at 30 September 2026: NAV Rs 111.51 a share; unit trusts Rs 1,445mn, deposits Rs 956mn, listed shares Rs 120mn; stock Rs 973mn (Rs 606mn at March), receivables Rs 1,282mn (Rs 986mn); short-term loan Rs 200mn and overdraft Rs 21mn (none at March).
- Operating cash −Rs 456mn in the half (+Rs 565mn a year earlier). Dividend Rs 3.75 a share (Rs 158mn) paid 2 September 2026.
- 2025/26 (audited): revenue Rs 2,851mn (+17%), gross margin 31% (24%), profit Rs 798mn (+72%), EPS Rs 18.94, ROE 19.8%. Capex Rs 53mn, depreciation Rs 16mn.

**Valuation**

| Method | Bear | Base | Bull | Weighted |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DCF of PVC business + treasury | 122.81 | 150.03 | 176.87 | 147.23 |
| P/E (justified) | 82.15 | 104.35 | 136.88 | 104.20 |
| Justified P/B | 77.63 | 109.09 | 151.20 | 108.07 |
| Residual income | 75.23 | 118.10 | 189.68 | 119.56 |
| Average | 89.46 | 120.39 | 163.66 | **119.77** |

Weights bear 30 / base 50 / bull 20. All four methods come from scripts/valuation.py.

**Assumptions and what would change them**

- Required return: risk-free 8.24% (12.24% bond less 4.0% default spread) + beta 0.98 × (4.2% + 6.08%) = 18.3%; bear 19.8%, bull 16.8%. WACC 18.0% (debt weight 3%). The beta is a provisional global sector figure; a lower beta would lift value most.
- Growth 3% / 5.5% / 6.5% for five years, then 4% / 4.5% / 5%. Supported growth from 2025/26 reinvestment is 4.8% (24.4% reinvested × 19.9% return on capital), so all three are within 2 points.
- PVC business profit after tax Rs 549mn / 621mn / 658mn (September quarter × 4 / 2025/26 / twelve months), counting gross profit less administrative costs only, so the unit-trust gains aren't counted twice. Return on new capital 20% / 25% / 30%.
- Treasury investments added at book, Rs 59.86 a share. Net debt Rs 0.21bn subtracted. 48–61% of DCF value comes after year five.
- EPS to March 2027 Rs 17.70 / 19.20 / 21.20; the base is 9.8% below the Rs 21.29 run-rate because the September quarter's margin and EPS fell.
- Long-run ROE 15% / 18% / 21%; payout 20%.
- Maintenance capex is about depreciation (Rs 16–27mn); 2025/26's Rs 53mn of capex was mostly upkeep and a vehicle, not growth. No growth project, no capital commitments.

**Risks**

- Customer concentration: the parent and its affiliate buy essentially everything at board-set prices, and owed Rs 815mn at March 2026 (plus a Rs 114mn loan to ACL Cables).
- Margin: PVC resin costs and the rupee; the September quarter's margin was 6 points lower.
- Cash: negative operating cash in the half; a second weak half would fail the cash test.
- About a quarter of 2025/26 profit before tax came from unit-trust, interest and exchange gains, which swing with markets.

**Buy plan (500 shares)**

| Tier | Shares | Up to |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 200 | Rs 101.80 |
| 2 | 150 | Rs 95.00 |
| 3 | 150 | Rs 89.80 |

Average about Rs 96.16, about Rs 48,080 in total (Rs 78,125 at today's price). Rs 101.80 is 35% below the price and below every trade since the December 2025 subdivision (low Rs 115.25 in 2025/26, Rs 135 in July–September 2026), so the plan needs a broad market fall or a clear setback.

**Watch next**: December 2026 quarter margin, whether stock and group receivables come down and the loan is repaid, sales outside the group, and the January 2027 beta refresh.

said.text: 2025/26 was the best year in the company's history: revenue +17% to Rs 2,851mn, profit +72% to Rs 798mn

Gross margin rose to 31% from 24% despite lower selling prices, through cost control and efficiency
Plants ran at peak efficiency; capacity utilisation 91% on output of 6,266 tonnes
Rising raw material prices, rupee weakness and global trade shifts are the risks for 2026/27

Dividend of Rs 3.75 a share for 2025/26, paid September 2026
